decline: That's outside what this site documents.

chunks.title: Variant Evidence Agent — what it does
chunks.answer: The Variant Evidence Agent performs calibrated VUS reclassification with an evidence-citing agent. For each variant of uncertain significance it retrieves the records behind a call and writes an evidence summary in which every claim is cited — under a hard rule: cite, or decline. Never invent. Where the evidence is not there, the answer is “insufficient evidence — remains VUS.”

chunks.title: web-agent — what it does
chunks.answer: web-agent is an autonomous agent that operates web interfaces end to end. It drives headless Chromium through a task suite with an observe → ground → act → verify → recover loop: take a fresh snapshot of the page, act on it, verify the result against the step's postcondition — and when the page fights back, re-ground and recover instead of failing silently.

chunks.title: web-agent — headline results
chunks.answer: With recovery on, web-agent passes 36/36 tasks — the full evaluation set. With recovery off, the same agent passes 27/36. The difference is the recovery system, measured as an ablation on the same 36 tasks.

chunks.title: web-agent — recovery off
keywords: what happens when recovery is off
chunks.answer: Recovery off disables all three recovery mechanisms — no re-grounding, no overlay dismissal, no retries — so the first failure ends the task. The same agent then passes 27/36 tasks: the 27 controls still pass, and all nine adversarial tasks fail (0/9).

chunks.title: web-agent — adversarial vs control tasks
chunks.answer: Nine of the 36 tasks are adversarial: the page mutates or obstructs mid-task — a button is renamed after a field is typed into, an overlay rises over the control, a same-label decoy appears. Adversarial tasks pass 9/9 with recovery on and 0/9 with it off. The 27 control tasks pass 27/27 both ways.

chunks.title: Variant Evidence Agent — final model scores
chunks.answer: The final model (GBM+R — gradient boosting + REVEL + isotonic, adopted 2026-10-26) reaches AUROC 0.970 on the post-freeze temporal test set, with calibration error (ECE) 0.025 and Brier 0.062. The trade-off is stated: its ECE is worse than the previously served Model 2's 0.017 — Model 2 stays the best-calibrated model in the record. Discrimination and calibration are reported as separate claims for every model variant.

chunks.title: Calibration — ECE of the final model
chunks.answer: The final model's expected calibration error is ECE 0.025 (AUROC 0.970, Brier 0.062). ECE is computed in 10 equal-width bins as the bin-size-weighted average gap between mean predicted probability and observed fraction pathogenic.

chunks.title: Variant Evidence Agent — the test set
chunks.answer: The temporal test set holds 27,748 variants that were uncertain at the Jan 2024 freeze and reclassified after it (8,856 pathogenic, 18,892 benign). The frozen training set holds 1,103,657 labelled variants. No test label existed at train time.

chunks.title: Variant Evidence Agent — summarised vs declined
chunks.answer: On the test set the agent summarises 10,357 variants (37.3%) with cited evidence and declines 17,391 (62.7%). A decline — “insufficient evidence — remains VUS” — is a designed output, not an error.

chunks.title: Evaluation method — how recovery works
chunks.answer: When a step fails — target not found, an action error, or a postcondition not met — recovery does three things. Re-grounding: the target is looked up again in a fresh snapshot with fallback strategies instead of the exact text or id. Overlay dismissal: if another element intercepts pointer events, the agent clicks the overlay's dismiss control and retries. Retry budget: at most 2 retries per step, then the task fails and the failure is reported as-is.

chunks.title: Calibration — isotonic vs Platt
chunks.answer: Two calibration maps are compared: Platt scaling and isotonic regression, each fitted on train data only — never on the test set. Platt fitted on the training window made probabilities worse on the temporal test (ECE 0.040 uncalibrated → 0.157). Isotonic calibration fitted on the train holdout is the map the final model ships, at ECE 0.025.

chunks.title: Calibration — per-gene, worst first
chunks.answer: Calibration is reported per gene for the 24 genes with n ≥ 50 scored test variants, ordered worst first. 23 sit between 0.005 and 0.154; USH2A, at 0.204, is a calibration failure by the project's own standard and stays in the table.

chunks.title: Temporal evaluation — the freeze/test design
chunks.answer: Classifications are frozen at the Jan 2024 cutoff: train on the 1,103,657 variants labelled at the cutoff, test only on the 27,748 variants reclassified after it. Random splits leak — a reclassified variant reappears, with the scores used to reclassify it as features, in both train and test. A near-duplicate guard removes test rows sharing gene + name with train; it removed 0 rows in this build.

chunks.title: Variant Evidence Agent — batch pack
chunks.answer: Submit a set of variants and receive an evidence pack: one cited summary per variant that clears the evidence bar, with each remaining variant declined individually rather than summarised on thin evidence. On the temporal test set the agent summarises 10,357 of 27,748 variants and declines 17,391.

chunks.title: Variant Evidence Agent — single lookup
chunks.answer: Enter one variant and read its stored report: the calibrated probability from the final model and the evidence summary in which every claim is cited to a retrieved record — or an explicit decline, “insufficient evidence — remains VUS”, where the evidence is not there.

chunks.title: Variant Evidence Agent — live-evidence mode
chunks.answer: In live-evidence mode the agent gathers the records that bear on a variant and applies the same rule — cite, or decline. A minimum of 3 distinct evidence items is required before the agent says anything at all; below that, the verdict is fixed: “insufficient evidence — remains VUS.”

chunks.title: web-agent — how to use
chunks.answer: Pick one of the 36 fixture tasks (or point the agent at a public page in the live session), run it with recovery on, then toggle recovery off and run the same task again. The results panel reports pass or fail against the task's step postconditions, with attempts and recoveries counted; the trace shows every step — observe, ground, act, verify, and each recovery — with screenshots along the way.

chunks.title: Variant Evidence Agent — limits
chunks.answer: This is a research system, not a certified medical product, and not for clinical use: a calibrated probability is not a clinical classification, and ACMG classification remains a human, guideline-driven judgement. Coverage is partial by construction — the predictor scores are missense-only and precomputed, covering 37.4% of the test set — and the evaluation labels themselves are partly predictor-influenced.

chunks.title: The recovery ablation — limits
chunks.answer: The web-agent evaluation runs on the project's own test pages: deterministic local fixture pages in headless Chromium, styled as real product surfaces rather than bare HTML. The suite is 36 tasks on those pages — the results are claims about that fixture scope, measured exactly, and not claims about arbitrary live websites.

chunks.title: Evaluation method — scoring rules
chunks.answer: Every step of every task carries an explicit postcondition written against the page: visible text, row counts, field values, checked state. A task passes only when every step's postcondition holds — no partial credit. Each run writes a raw run file recording success, steps, attempts, recoveries used, and the recorded error for a failure. In Evaluation v1.0, total attempts were 185 with recovery on and 171 off.

chunks.title: The recovery ablation — the nine failures
chunks.answer: With recovery on there are no failures to list. With it off, the run file records nine failures — all adversarial tasks. The recorded errors fall into three kinds: target_not_found (renamed targets never found), action_error timeouts (covered buttons' clicks timed out), and verify_failed (decoys failed their postconditions). The article lists each task with its recorded error string, verbatim.

chunks.title: hybrid-perturb-bench — what it is
chunks.answer: hybrid-perturb-bench is an honest benchmark for perturbation-response prediction on Norman et al. 2019 Perturb-seq (CRISPRa, K562): 111,445 cells × 33,694 genes, 105 single perturbations and 131 combinations, scored on the top 2000 evaluation genes with 21 entire perturbations held out against 84 train singles.

chunks.title: hybrid-perturb-bench — held-out singles result
chunks.answer: On held-out single perturbations the hybrid does not beat the baselines it was built to challenge: Pearson Δ 0.5366 and DEG overlap 0.3143, below the global perturbation mean (0.5876 Pearson, 0.3314 overlap) and the linear ridge (0.5785). It improves only on no-change (MSE 0.005134 vs 0.006534) and on its own retrieval channel (0.5076 Pearson). The negative result is reported as-is.

chunks.title: hybrid-perturb-bench — combinations
chunks.answer: On the 131 combinations — never used in any training — the picture reverses: additive_hybrid reaches Pearson Δ 0.8248 and the direct hybrid 0.7995, far above the global mean (0.5663) and the ridge (0.5753), though below the split-half ceiling (0.9314). One flag: additive_hybrid's both-train subgroup is partly in-sample, because the hybrid was trained on those singles.

chunks.title: hybrid-perturb-bench — GEARS comparator
chunks.answer: GEARS was attempted as a comparator and not completed: the run stopped inside GEARS' per-cell graph construction, before training began. No GEARS predictions exist and no GEARS numbers are reported anywhere in the project's results — nothing in the benchmark is a statement about GEARS' accuracy.

chunks.title: web-agent — downloads and Evaluation v1.0
chunks.answer: The current result set is labelled Evaluation v1.0 — the 36-task suite with both modes run. Its raw outputs ship with this site from the web-agent page: results/run_on.json (36/36 passed), results/run_off.json (27/36 passed) and RESULTS.md, byte-identical to the lab's own copies.

chunks.title: Omevra — contact
chunks.answer: Use the Contact section on the Omevra home page — it links to LinkedIn, which is the fastest route for questions about the systems, the methods, or the results. This site does not publish an email address.

chunks.title: Methods library — overview
chunks.answer: The methods library documents how the results were produced, in the projects' own terms: Evaluation (the ablation design and scoring rules), Calibration (isotonic calibration and per-gene reporting, worst first), and Temporal evaluation (the freeze/test design behind the variant results). Each product page links to all three.

chunks.title: web-agent architecture — the state machine
chunks.answer: web-agent's loop is a state machine in src/agent.py: for each step, observe (a fresh DOM snapshot from src/snapshot.py, every element with a ref and a locator recipe), ground (exact semantic match on role plus text, label or name), act, then verify the step's postcondition. A failure is classified — target_not_found, action_error or verify_failed — logged, and, with recovery on, answered by re-grounding or overlay dismissal inside a budget of at most 2 retries per step. Every action carries a 3,000 ms timeout, and verification polls for up to 2.0 s.

chunks.title: web-agent architecture — public-page rails
chunks.answer: The public-page mode treats the visitor's URL, label and text as untrusted. Before any browsing, validate_public_url (src/public_mode.py) accepts only http(s), refuses localhost and .local names, and checks every address the host resolves to — one private, loopback, link-local, reserved, multicast or unspecified address refuses the URL. Only two fixed intents exist, capped at 2 steps. A route guard aborts navigation to a different registrable domain, and the domain is re-checked before and after every step. Password fields, and fields matching a payment term, are never typed into; downloads are disabled.

chunks.title: Variant Evidence Agent architecture — model vs code
chunks.answer: The Variant Evidence Agent's model decides one thing: the calibrated probability, from the stored model prediction (GBM+R since 2026-10-26). Everything else is enforced in code. Evidence is assembled only from prediction-time records (AlphaMissense, the ClinVar status frozen at the cutoff, the gene prior), each carrying its record id; assess requires at least 3 distinct evidence items and a probability, or the report declines with the fixed verdict “insufficient evidence — remains VUS”. Every claim in a report carries its record id — there is no path for an uncited claim into a report.

chunks.title: Variant Evidence Agent architecture — live-evidence boundaries
chunks.answer: For a variant outside the scored universe the system does not extrapolate: live-evidence mode retrieves current records — ClinVar via NCBI E-utilities (the top 5 records) and gnomAD via its GraphQL API, which needs GRCh38 coordinates — and returns them as retrieved, labelled “Live retrieved evidence”, with no model score attached. Every failure is reported as a status (ok, not_found, failed, unavailable) with its reason; content is never invented to fill a gap.

chunks.title: Variant Evidence Agent architecture — the batch flow
chunks.answer: A batch is a pasted list of variants, or one gene name expanding to all its variants in the scored universe. Input is de-duplicated and capped at 20,000 characters; a batch resolving to more than 25 variants is rejected with a clear message, never truncated. Each variant runs the single-variant code path — in the universe, the agent report; outside it, live-evidence mode — with external calls serialised behind a lock, at least 0.5 s apart. The pack counts summarised, declined and live-evidence outcomes separately.

chunks.title: Tools — the directory
chunks.answer: The tools directory lists every usable tool in one place: the variant report (one variant, cited or declined), the batch evidence pack (paste a list, expand a gene, or upload a variant-list file), the variant normaliser (any spelling in — the cleaned form and its universe status out), the gene explorer (one gene's counts, its published calibration where one exists, and its variants), web-agent's live run and public-page mode, and Ask Omevra itself. Completed batches are also listed under Recent batches in the visitor's own browser — saved on that device, not on a server.

chunks.title: Tools — literature panel (PubMed)
chunks.answer: Live-evidence mode also retrieves literature: for the variant being looked up, the agent searches PubMed and shows the matching records — title, journal, year and a linked PMID — as retrieved citations, alongside the current ClinVar and gnomAD records. Retrieval only: no score is attached and nothing is claimed about what a paper concludes; when the lookup cannot be completed, the panel says the literature lookup is unavailable.

chunks.title: NGS Pipeline Atlas — what it is
chunks.answer: The NGS Pipeline Atlas is a reproducible Nextflow pipeline for bacterial whole-genome sequencing: paired-end reads in, per-sample QC-gated variant calls out. It ran on ENA study PRJNA234495 — Escherichia coli K-12 resequencing — against the MG1655 reference NC_000913.3, through MD5-verified fetch, a read-pair sanitize stage, FastQC and fastp, BWA-MEM alignment, per-sample QC gates, bcftools calling, and a cohort report written by the project's own Python.

chunks.title: NGS Pipeline Atlas — the QC gates and the cohort outcome
chunks.answer: The gates are fixed thresholds set before the cohort run: mean coverage at least 10.0x, at least 80% of reads mapped, at least 70% Q30 bases. Of 33 samples attempted, 27 passed all three gates and went on to variant calling; 6 stopped, every one on the coverage gate — the deliberate bad input BADINPUT01 at 0.01x and five genuine samples between 8.82x and 9.99x. A stopped sample's BAM is removed inside the gate step and it is never called.

chunks.title: NGS Pipeline Atlas — reproducibility and the sanitize stage
chunks.answer: The pipeline was executed twice end to end in fully separate directories, with no result reused from the first run's cache. The two cohort reports are byte-identical (MD5 822aad36…), all 27 per-sample variant tables are byte-identical, and the sanitize totals match exactly: 27,175,960 read pairs processed, 104,684 corrupt pairs dropped (0.39%) — corruption found inside the archive's own MD5-authentic files and removed at read level.

chunks.title: Multi-Agent Evidence — what it is
chunks.answer: Multi-Agent Evidence splits genetic-variant evidence work across three agents in a LangGraph state graph: a deterministic Retriever assembles the evidence packet for a variant, a Synthesiser drafts the summary as cited claims from the packet (or declines when the gate is not met), and a Critic checks every drafted claim against the packet, sending rejected drafts back for revision. A deterministic finalise step enforces the cite-or-decline gate in code: gate not met, the output is the decline, and any claim citing a record outside the packet is removed.

chunks.title: Multi-Agent Evidence — the comparison result
keywords: multi-agent system beat the single-agent baseline
chunks.answer: On the fixed set of 36 variants the multi-agent system did not beat the single-agent baseline on any quality axis: citation accuracy 1.00 vs 1.00 after the manual audit, completeness 1.00 vs 1.00, and decline correctness 36/36 for both. The multi-agent system used 46,225 tokens against the baseline's 17,062 and 3.74 s mean latency per variant against 1.40 s — 2.7 times the cost for the same scores. The tie is the published finding.

chunks.title: Multi-Agent Evidence — what the critic did, and the failure modes
chunks.answer: Across the 36 variants the critic ran 47 rounds and rejected drafts 16 times: 13 rejections policed out-of-universe drafts that treated a live record as if it could carry a summary, and 3 were false positives on one variant's wording. In the failure-mode exercises the loop caught a sabotaged draft whose false ACMG PS3 claim carried a valid-looking citation — the case the code guard alone cannot detect. One design gap is recorded: when frozen and live records conflict, no agent owns raising the disagreement, so the conflict passes silently.
